def-linear-process-and-arma-model:
## Definition

Let $X=(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a real process on one probability space.
The backshift is $(BX)_t:=X_{t-1}$, and for a polynomial
$a(z)=\sum_{j=0}^m a_jz^j$ set
$a(B)X_t:=\sum_{j=0}^m a_jX_{t-j}$. Weak stationarity and the covariance
convention are those of
[[def-strict-and-weak-stationarity-for-time-series]] and
[[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]].

A real process $\epsilon=(\epsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is **white noise**
with variance $\sigma^2$ when
$\mathbb E[\epsilon_t]=0$, $0<\sigma^2=\mathbb E[\epsilon_t^2]<\infty$,
and $\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon_t,\epsilon_s)=0$ for all $s\ne t$.
This definition requires only zero covariance at distinct times; it does not
require independence, identical distributions, or Gaussian laws.

For a real sequence $\psi=(\psi_j)_{j\ge0}$ with
$\sum_{j\ge0}|\psi_j|<\infty$, a **causal linear process** driven by white
noise is
$$X_t-\mu:=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\psi_j\epsilon_{t-j},\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
where the series is its almost-sure and $L^2$ limit, established by
[[lem-absolutely-summable-linear-filters-preserve-weak-stationarity]].

An **ARMA$(p,q)$ model**, for nonnegative integers $p,q$, is an equation
$$\phi(B)(X_t-\mu)=\theta(B)\epsilon_t,\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
where
$$\phi(z)=1-\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_jz^j,\qquad \theta(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^q\theta_jz^j$$
have real coefficients and constant term one. If $p=0$ or $q=0$, the
corresponding polynomial is $1$. First cancel every common nonconstant factor
of $\phi$ and $\theta$ in $\mathbb C[z]$, then normalize both remaining
polynomials to have constant term one. Thus the model uses a **coprime
normalized pair**, meaning that the two polynomials have no common complex
root and both have constant term one.

For an AR$(p)$ model ($q=0$), expansion gives the regression form
$X_t=c+\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_jX_{t-j}+\epsilon_t$ with
$c=\mu(1-\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_j)$. Thus a fixed intercept in the AR regression
is the original mean parameter written in observation coordinates.

A **causal representation** of this model is a representation
$X_t-\mu=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_j\epsilon_{t-j}$ with
$\sum_j|\psi_j|<\infty$. An **invertible representation** is
$\epsilon_t=\sum_{j\ge0}\pi_j(X_{t-j}-\mu)$ with
$\sum_j|\pi_j|<\infty$. These are properties of the displayed relation
between $X$ and $\epsilon$, not claims that white noise is iid.
lem-absolutely-summable-linear-filters-p:
## Statement

Let $Z=(Z_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered real weakly stationary process
with autocovariance $\gamma$. For a real two-sided sequence
$c=(c_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ define
$c(B)Z_t:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}c_jZ_{t-j}$. Then this filter is well-defined
almost surely and in $L^2$, is centered and weakly stationary, and has
autocovariance
$$\gamma_Y(h)=\sum_{j,k\in\mathbb Z}c_jc_k\gamma(h-j+k),\qquad h\in\mathbb Z.$$
For $c,d\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ their filter composition is the convolution
filter
$$(c*d)_m:=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}c_jd_{m-j},\qquad c(B)\bigl(d(B)Z\bigr)=(c*d)(B)Z.$$
All sums are absolutely convergent in the senses justified below. This
argument uses no choice axiom.
thm-arma-causality-and-invertibility-roo:
## Statement

Let $X$ be weakly stationary and let $(X_t,\epsilon_t)$ satisfy the
normalized coprime ARMA$(p,q)$ equation
of [[def-linear-process-and-arma-model]], with centered white noise of
variance $\sigma^2>0$. A **causal representation** with absolutely summable
one-sided coefficients exists if and only if $\phi(z)\ne0$ for every
$|z|\le1$. In that case its coefficients are uniquely determined by
$$\Psi(z):=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_jz^j=\frac{\theta(z)}{\phi(z)},\qquad |z|\le1,$$
and there are constants $C<\infty$ and $r>1$ with
$|\psi_j|\le Cr^{-j}$.

An **invertible representation** with absolutely summable one-sided
coefficients exists if and only if $\theta(z)\ne0$ for every $|z|\le1$. Its
coefficients are uniquely determined by
$$\Pi(z):=\sum_{j\ge0}\pi_jz^j=\frac{\phi(z)}{\theta(z)},\qquad |z|\le1.$$
The two criteria are separate: neither condition assumes the other.
thm-stationary-arma-spectral-density:
## Statement

Let $X_t-\mu$ be a real weakly stationary solution of the normalized coprime
ARMA$(p,q)$ equation
$$\phi(B)(X_t-\mu)=\theta(B)\epsilon_t,$$
where $\epsilon$ is centered white noise with variance $\sigma^2>0$. If
$\phi(z)\ne0$ for every $|z|=1$, then $X$ has a spectral density, under the
convention
$\gamma(h)=\int_{\mathbb T}e^{ih\lambda}F(d\lambda)$ and angular Lebesgue
measure $d\lambda$ of total mass $2\pi$, given by
$$f(\lambda)=\frac{\sigma^2}{2\pi}\frac{|\theta(e^{-i\lambda})|^2}{|\phi(e^{-i\lambda})|^2},\qquad -\pi\le\lambda\le\pi.$$
No causal or invertible root condition is required; zeros of $\theta$ on the
unit circle are permitted.
thm-stable-linear-process-sample-mean-cl:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let
$$X_t-\mu=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_j\epsilon_{t-j},\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
be a causal linear process with real coefficients satisfying
$\sum_{j\ge0}\sqrt{j+1}\,|\psi_j|<\infty$. Suppose the two-sided innovation
sequence $(\epsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is iid, centered, and has
$0<\sigma^2=\mathbb E[\epsilon_0^2]<\infty$. Put
$\Psi:=\sum_{j\ge0}\psi_j$ and
$\bar X_n:=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t$. Then
$$\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2\Psi^2).$$
For a causal ARMA model with no zero of $\phi$ in $|z|\le1$, the root
criterion theorem implies that its coefficients satisfy the weighted
summability condition. The limiting variance may be zero when $\Psi=0$.
If $\tau^2:=\sigma^2\Psi^2>0$ and a nonnegative variance estimate
$\widehat\tau_n^2$ separately satisfies
$\widehat\tau_n^2\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}\tau^2$, then
$T_n:=\sqrt n(\bar X_n-\mu)/\widehat\tau_n$,
with $\widehat\tau_n=\sqrt{\widehat\tau_n^2}$ and any finite convention
when $\widehat\tau_n=0$, converges to $N(0,1)$. For each fixed $c>0$, the
symmetric interval
$$\left[\bar X_n-\frac{c\widehat\tau_n}{\sqrt n}, \bar X_n+\frac{c\widehat\tau_n}{\sqrt n}\right]$$
therefore has limiting coverage $\mathbb P(|N(0,1)|\le c)$. No consistency
is attributed to a variance estimator unless it is separately proved.
thm-fixed-order-autoregressive-ols-marti:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $p\ge1$, put
$\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p)^T$, and let
$Y_t=(X_{t-1},\ldots,X_{t-p})^T$. Either take $Z_t=Y_t$ and
$X_t=\beta^TZ_t+\epsilon_t$ with $d=p$ and $\beta=\phi$, or take
$Z_t=(1,Y_t^T)^T$ and $X_t=\beta^TZ_t+\epsilon_t$ with $d=p+1$ to include
a fixed intercept. Let $X$ be a strictly stationary process whose canonical
one-sided shift is ergodic, and suppose the displayed AR($p$) equation holds.
Assume the innovations $(\epsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ are iid, centered, have
$0<\sigma^2=\mathbb E[\epsilon_0^2]<\infty$, and are independent of the past:
for the filtration
$$\mathcal F_t:=\sigma(X_s,\epsilon_s:s\le t),\qquad t\in\mathbb N_0,$$
$Z_t$ is $\mathcal F_{t-1}$-measurable and $\epsilon_t$ is independent of
$\mathcal F_{t-1}$ for each $t\ge1$. Assume
$$\Gamma:=\mathbb E[Z_tZ_t^T]$$
is finite and positive definite, meaning $a^T\Gamma a>0$ for every
$a\ne0$.

For observations at $t=1,\ldots,n$, set
$$G_n:=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n}Z_tZ_t^T,\qquad b_n:=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n}Z_tX_t.$$
Define the measurable OLS fallback by $\widehat\beta_n=G_n^{-1}b_n$ when
$G_n$ is invertible and $\widehat\beta_n=0$ otherwise, and define
$$\widehat\sigma_n^2:=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^{n} (X_t-\widehat\beta_n^TZ_t)^2.$$
Then
$$\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta)\Rightarrow N_d(0,\sigma^2\Gamma^{-1}),\qquad \widehat\sigma_n^2\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}\sigma^2.$$
If $W_n$ is the fixed-order Wald statistic
$$W_n:=\frac{n}{\widehat\sigma_n^2} (\widehat\beta_n-\beta)^TG_n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta)$$
when $G_n$ is invertible and $\widehat\sigma_n^2>0$, and is set to $0$
otherwise, then $W_n\Rightarrow\chi_d^2$. These statements use fixed $p$;
they do not assert validity after data-selected order.
cor-stable-ar-long-run-variance-plug-in-:
## Statement

Assume AC and fix $p\ge1$. Let $X$ be a stable AR$(p)$ with unknown mean $\mu$,
$$X_t-\mu=\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_j(X_{t-j}-\mu)+\epsilon_t,$$
with iid centered innovations of variance $0<\sigma^2<\infty$. Assume the
strict stationarity, ergodicity, past independence, and positive-definite
augmented Gram hypotheses of
[[thm-fixed-order-autoregressive-ols-martingale-limit]], using its
fixed-intercept regressor $Z_t=(1,X_{t-1},\ldots,X_{t-p})^T$ and coefficient
vector $(c,\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p)^T$ with
$c=\mu(1-\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_j)$. Write $\widehat\phi_n$ for the OLS slope
vector and $\widehat\sigma_n^2$ for its residual mean square. Define
$$\widehat\tau_n^2:= \begin{cases} \widehat\sigma_n^2/(1-\sum_{j=1}^p\widehat\phi_{n,j})^2, &1-\sum_j\widehat\phi_{n,j}\ne0,\\ 0,&1-\sum_j\widehat\phi_{n,j}=0. \end{cases}$$
Then
$$\widehat\tau_n^2\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P} \frac{\sigma^2}{(1-\sum_{j=1}^p\phi_j)^2} =\sigma^2\Psi^2>0,$$
where $\Psi$ is the coefficient sum of the causal AR$(p)$ representation.
Consequently $\widehat\tau_n^2$ supplies the consistent positive variance
scale required by
[[thm-stable-linear-process-sample-mean-clt]] for the sample-mean interval.
